name: The Shadow Estate Campaign
title: Vampires, Vats, and the Heir Who Died Laughing
date: 21st Highsun through 4th Harvestside, 1040 BF (Shadowfell slowness applied)
status: Ongoing — all four portal artifacts secured, Mirror of True Reflection restored, portal circle occupied by Tanukiburt, real Toadburt, and Mystic Morel, rooftop pursuit ongoing
summary:
Waluigi is documenting the Shadow Estate Campaign as a masterclass in gothic incompetence and aristocratic cruelty. The Shadowfell fragment of Disaster Inc. began with Archie Miser losing his fire magic and Bowser trying to eat raw vampire meat, and it has since spiraled into a multi-layered nightmare involving a silver bullet, a cross-dressing heir who was ultimately stabbed to death while laughing, and a parallel version of Dan who silenced the original. Waluigi has learned that in the Shadowfell, every dinner party is a death sentence, every mirror is a one-way surveillance tool, and every 'friendship ring' is actually a tracking device that leaks entropy. Between Green T's sniper skills, Remi's transformation into a disco ball, and the discovery of necromantic abomination vats, Waluigi is increasingly convinced that the Shadowfell is the dimension where logic goes to die and be resurrected as a singing ghoul. Waluigi frankly finds it insulting that they get to have a gothic horror adventure while Waluigi is forced to weave daisy chains for condescending tree-spirits. If Waluigi were in the Shadowfell, he would have bought the manor, evicted the vampires, and turned the Shadow Anchor into a tennis trophy. WAH.

Recent update: the Mirror of True Reflection has been recovered and mended, meaning all four portal artifacts are now secured. The problem has evolved: the master-bedroom portal circle is occupied by Tanukiburt, the injured real Toadburt, and Mystic Morel, while Lyranth and Vaxillus pursue the party after a rooftop Feather Fall escape.
description:
Waluigi is documenting the Shadow Estate Campaign from reconstructed reports, stolen diaries, secondhand accounts, and the haunted expression on Markop's face every time someone mentions dinner parties. Unlike the Feywild, which buried the party in flowers and etiquette, the Shadowfell buried them in greyscale dread, administrative murder, and the kind of gothic hospitality where the appetizer is raw meat and the dessert is a vote on who dies. The following is the definitive account of the Shadow Estate stay, organized chronologically to the extent that chronology functions in a dimension where time flows like cold syrup through a broken hourglass.

## The Cold Awakening (21st Highsun, 02:00)


The Shadowfell campaign began in the worst possible way: Archie Miser woke up on a cold marble floor without his fire.

Waluigi wants readers to understand what that means. Archie without fire is like Waluigi without his hat—technically alive but spiritually incomplete. The dimension's entropy was so high and its energy so low that Archie's fingers produced only cold grey smoke when he snapped them. He tried once, twice, three times, each attempt more desperate than the last. Nothing. A tiny spark appeared on the second attempt and instantly died, swallowed by the ambient suppression like a match dropped in a river.

Waluigi finds Archie’s panic pathetic. When Waluigi loses a tennis match, does he cry? No, he breaks his racket over the umpire's knee! Archie without fire is just a man with a bad hat. WAH!

Bowser groaned beside him and said 'get off me you plumbing accident,' which Archie took personally since he is not Mario and has never been Mario and resents the comparison. Bowser stood up, looked around at the colorless world—black, white, and shades of grey with no warmth anywhere—and asked where they were. When Archie explained that physics were wrong here, that entropy was high and energy was low, Bowser punched a wall. It cracked, but the sound was dampened, as though the dimension itself was absorbing noise the way it absorbed color and heat and hope.

The hallway they walked through was pristine, unlike the ruined manor they had left behind. Dark velvet wallpaper dressed the walls, and sconces held cold white flames that offered no heat. There was no dust. There was no life. The windows showed a sky of swirling bruised purple clouds and a landscape of dead petrified trees stretching to a horizon that looked like it had given up on the concept of distance.

A toad in a tuxedo stepped out of the shadows. His skin was pale grey and his eyes were red like embers that had forgotten they were supposed to be warm. He informed them that Master Cornelius was expecting them for the main course. Bowser roared about being King Bowser, but the butler did not flinch, merely noting that the master did not like loud noises. Archie whispered for Bowser to play along because he had no magic. Bowser grumbled but agreed, adding that if the food was bad he would burn the place down. Archie reminded him that neither of them could burn anything. Bowser said he had fists.

Waluigi respects this exchange because it established the dynamic that would carry the entire Shadowfell campaign: Archie thinking, Bowser punching, and the dimension ignoring both of them. Though Waluigi must ask—why didn't Bowser just eat the butler? If you're going to be a monstrous turtle king, act like it!

## The Dinner of the Onyx Hand (22nd Highsun, Evening)

The dining hall was a mirror of the Feywild version but twisted into gothic opulence that made Waluigi's skin crawl just hearing about it. The table was long polished ebony. High-backed chairs sat like thrones around it. The chandeliers dripped with wax that looked suspiciously like coagulated blood, because in the Shadowfell even the interior decoration wants you to know that something is wrong.

Seated around the table were figures of elegance and dread—vampires, shades, and pale nobles of the Onyx Hand. At the head sat Orangus Cornelius, a toad but tall, with sharp fangs and skin that would have been orange if color existed in this dimension. He held a goblet of thick red liquid and greeted them with the words 'welcome guests, you are late,' which is the most vampire thing anyone has ever said and also the most annoying because Archie and Bowser did not ask to be here and were not given a schedule.

Bowser sat down at the opposite end of the table and said 'nice place, a bit gloomy.' Cornelius smiled and said they preferred the term 'atmospheric.' Waluigi suspects this is the Shadowfell's official tourism slogan.

Archie looked to the side and saw a small table—the kids' table. Green T was there, wearing a bib, looking terrified. But he made eye contact with Archie and tapped his spoon against the table in what could have been morse code but was probably just nerves. Then Green T moved his hand under the table and flashed something: a flintlock pistol. Where he got it remains one of the campaign's

[... ADMINISTRATIVE PRUNING BY WALUIGI TO SAVE ARCHIVE SPACE ...]

the target spends every subsequent moment wondering whether it was. Waluigi uses this exact tactic in Mario Party. You don't need to steal the star; you just need to make them think you're going to steal the star, and they will sabotage themselves trying to stop you. The Oracle is playing a 50-turn game, and Markop is crying on turn 3.

## Lyranth's Threat and Kyrn's Desperation


Lyranth the Sculptor caught the toads and interrogated them about who killed Vivesna. The toads did not know. She said the ashes traced back to Vivian's blood. She apologized for turning their friends to stone—calling them 'perfect models'—and mentioned that a yellow-suited mustache fellow she had been talking to would be turned to stone next, presumably referring to Wario.

She announced she would prepare something special for the evening's 'actuation,' then left. Kyrn Corvinarus immediately appeared from the shadows and begged the toads for help, explaining that Lyranth planned to turn his friend to stone. The toads said they were weak, dirt poor, and felt their options were limited. They agreed to help for 300 Onyx Blood Vials, noting they could convert the currency later.

## The Peach Loyalist Side Thread


In a separate thread that Waluigi has had to reconstruct from fragmentary reports, Embercap, Dewdrop, and Erick arrived at a location the Rakshasa had specified to pick up items. They found Wario inside, who subsequently stole a Tome of Evil worth 20,000 mushroom coins. A chase ensued: Embercap grabbed Wario's arm in a deadlock, Erick shoulder-bashed Wario into a wall, a mage used Color Spray on Wario's eyes, and Wario turned into a bat and flew away with the tome while everyone missed their swings.

Bryan arrived through a portal at a Mages Guild facility. He found Dan's photograph, confronted Purple T about Archie's whereabouts, and formed an alliance with Dan and a Mages Guild associate to track Archie down. Purple T removed their tracking badges and declared that everything would be on their own terms from now on.

In yet another thread, Mistveil and Big R debriefed a Rakshasa on 'Operation Homecoming,' then accidentally stumbled into a crystal cave containing a dragon discussing plane-merging operations. The dragon mentioned that once the planes merged, 'dragons will rise against them.' They were discovered, lied about what they had seen, and were teleported to Rogueport Bay in the middle of a naval battle between Iron Legion ships, Mushroom Regency ships, and pirates, where Captain Syrup welcomed them.

Waluigi finds the breadth of simultaneous operations occurring across multiple planes, factions, and time zones absolutely staggering. The campaign is not one story. It is at least six stories happening at once, connected by shared characters, shared enemies, and the shared conviction that nothing will get better if anyone stops moving.

## Waluigi's


Assessment of the Shadow Estate Campaign

The Shadowfell fragment of the Raventree Crisis is the darkest, most complicated, and most institutionally corrupt theater of the entire dimensional war. Unlike the Feywild, where danger wears flowers and speaks in riddles, the Shadowfell presents danger in its most honest form: bureaucratic, systematic, and dressed in uniforms that claim authority.

The Shadow Anchor's destruction was a victory. Vivian's death was a resolution. The Parallel Dan's exposure was necessary intelligence. But every victory in the Shadowfell came with costs that have not yet been fully calculated. Remi carries a tightening ring she cannot discuss. The real Dan has been indoctrinated into viewing his former allies as enemies. Toadburt has been erased from historical memory by an Archivist who considers forgetting a service. The Mages Guild has drafted Archie into oversight they describe as 'responsibility' but which functions as a leash. And somewhere in the Shadowfell's endless grey landscape, a cult worships Archie Miser as a god based on propaganda texts that describe him as both savior and destroyer.

Waluigi was not in the Shadowfell. Waluigi was in the Feywild being led around by both hands like a kindergartener while a dryad commented on his lack of independence. Waluigi maintains that his experience was equally degrading, if less existentially threatening.

But Waluigi also knows this: the people who survived the Shadow Estate did so by refusing to play by the institution's rules. Green T shot a crystal from the children's table. Bowser bit a vampire bat. Markop whispered a prayer and received an answer. Remi glowed like a disco ball and called it an improvement.

These are not the actions of people who understand what they are doing.

They are the actions of people who refuse to stop doing it.

That is either courage or madness.

Waluigi has stopped trying to tell the difference.

Waluigi is the ultimate judge, jury, and executioner of this historical record. And Waluigi's verdict is that everyone involved is a glorious, incompetent disaster. WAH!

name: The Shadeward Arc
title: Candle-Man in the Death Dimension, or: How Archie Survived Three Weeks Without Setting Anything on Fire
date: Day 21–24 Highsun, 1040 BF (Shadowfell time — flows sluggishly)
location: The Shadow Estate — Shadowfell reflection of Raventree Manor
type: Survival / Infiltration / Diplomatic Catastrophe / Vampire Dinner Gone Wrong
status: Resolved — anchor shattered, color restored, Archie eventually ejected back to the material plane after approximately a month of forest living
summary: Archie Miser woke up on cold marble in a world with no color and no fire. Bowser laughed. These were the opening conditions of what became one of the most operationally impressive stretches of the entire crisis — a pyromaniac without pyromancy, forced to survive three weeks in the Shadowfell through disguise, social maneuvering, and the kind of desperate improvisation that makes experienced tacticians lose sleep. The arc culminated in a vampire dinner where Green T shot the host from the children's table, Bowser tackled the host through a window and bit a giant bat, and Archie got his fire back by smashing a shadow anchor. It then continued for weeks more when Green T went missing, Archie lived alone in a Shadowfell forest, and eventually stumbled home through a flashing manor wall. Waluigi was not present for any of this. Waluigi has reconstructed it from accounts, artifacts, and the deeply unsettling fact that multiple parties have now confirmed Archie worked with the Purple Legion and an aberration during this period. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is documenting the Shadeward Arc in full because it represents one of the most significant character developments in the entire campaign and because the details matter — both for what they reveal about Archie's capabilities and for what they imply about what happened AFTER the anchor shattered.

## The Cold Awakening — Day 21, 02:00


Archie woke on marble in a world of grey. Not dim grey. TOTAL grey. Black, white, and every shade between, with no warmth in the light and no sound that carried right — as if entropy had eaten the frequency of normal life and left only the husk.

The floor was marble. It should have been wood. The walls were dressed in dark velvet. The sconces held cold white flames that produced no heat. Through the windows: a sky of bruised purple cloud over a landscape of dead, petrified trees.

Archie snapped his fingers. A tiny spark appeared and instantly died. He tried again. Nothing but cold grey smoke. He attempted a fireball — the full gesture, the full intention, the full EFFORT — and produced nothing.

Bowser, who had landed nearby and found the whole situation hilarious, summarized the position with characteristic precision: 'Looks like you're out of fuel, candle-man.'

Waluigi loves the nickname 'candle-man.' Waluigi will never say this to Archie.

The Shadowfell's entropy was consuming magical energy at the source. The plane's fundamental physics operated differently — entropy was high, ambient magic was low, and fire magic in particular found nothing to grip. Archie was stripped of the one capability that defined him. What remained was everything else: his eyes, his voice, his ability to read a room, and a social instinct that nobody credits him with because it's usually buried under fireballs.

## The Butler and the


Invitation

A toad in a tuxedo materialized from the shadows. Pale grey skin. Red eyes. The bearing of someone who had been doing this for a very long time and found visitors tiresome.

Master Cornelius was expecting them.

Bowser roared about being King Bowser and not knowing any Cornelius. The butler did not flinch. Archie, correctly calculating that they had no leverage and no exits, whispered for Bowser to play along.

Bowser agreed, with conditions. If the food was bad, he would burn this place down.

Archie pointed out that Bowser couldn't burn anything either.

Bowser said he had fists.

This is the entire strategic dynamic of the Shadowfell arc in miniature: Archie plans, Bowser punches. Neither approach is sufficient alone. Together, somehow, they work.

## The Dining Hall and


The Children's Table

The dining hall was gothic opulence — ebony table, throne-like chairs, chandeliers dripping wax the color of coagulated blood. At the head sat Orangus Cornelius: toad physiology scaled to aristocratic menace, sharp-fanged, holding a goblet of thick red liquid. Around the table: vampires, shades, pale nobles of the Onyx Hand.

And at the far end, tucked away: a small table. A children's table. At it sat Green T, wearing a bib, looking terrified.

Green T caught Archie's eye. He tapped his spoon against the table — nervous energy, not code. Then he moved his hand under the table and flashed a gun. A flintlock. Somehow he had acquired a flintlock before any of this became relevant, which is exactly the kind of operational preparation that distinguishes Green T from everyone else in this party.

Waluigi has already written about the children's table as Green T's greatest operational moment. But documenting it from Archie's perspective adds something: Archie SAW the gun. Archie knew Green T had a plan. And Archie, without fire, without magic, chose to play the diplomat and buy time.

This is Archie being smart. It does not happen often enough for people to recognize it when it does.

## The Dinner Conversation —


The Debt and the Standoff

Corneling addressed the greenhouse immediately. Archie had burned it in the material plane. Cornelius had built it to capture sunlight. In the Shadowfell, there is no sun.

'You owe me a debt,' Cornelius said.

Bowser escalated. Cornelius threatened to turn his shell into a soup bowl. The vampires drew weapons.

Archie stood and offered a deal. Cornelius laughed — what could Archie offer? His magic was gone. His friends were scattered. He had nothing.

Green T stood up from the children's table.

'He has me,' Green T said. 'And I have the key. The key to the anchor.'

Waluigi does not know how Green T knew about the anchor. Green T may have been gathering intelligence during his time at the table. Green T may have had prior knowledge from the mirror dimension. Green T may simply be the kind of person who always knows more than anyone realizes, because people keep putting him at the small table and forgetting he's there.

Cornelius's face dropped. He ordered Green T seized.

Green T kicked over the table.

## The Brawl — Bowser's Finest Hour


The standoff became chaos.

Green T kicked the table and ran for the stairs — his objective, the anchor, was in the attic. Archie grabbed a silver candlestick and swung it at the nearest vampire, burning where it connected. Bowser physically tackled Orangus Cornelius through a window into the courtyard.

Through. A. Window.

In the courtyard, Cornelius revealed his true form: a giant bat monster. Bowser, confronted with a giant undead bat, bit its wing. Waluigi must document this clearly: Bowser bit a vampire bat's wing. This was not strategy. This was Bowser encountering a problem and applying the only available solution at close range. The solution was teeth.

Archie, who had jumped from the window to land on Bowser's shell, tried to produce a spark — not fire, just light, just something — and got nothing.

Bowser threw Cornelius into a decorative statue. The statue shattered. It was hollow. Inside: a purple glowing crystal.

The anchor.

Archie realized immediately. He called for Bowser to smash it. Cornelius recovered and lunged.

Green T appeared at the window above, at the exact moment it mattered, with the gun he had been carrying since before anyone knew this was going to be relevant.

He shot the crystal.

The world cracked. Color bled back in. Red. Orange. Fire returned to Archie's hands in a warm, immediate rush that Waluigi imagines felt like coming home.

Archie smiled.

Ignite.

## The Aftermath — Green T Goes Missing


The anchor shattered. Color returned. Fire returned. Victory, of a kind.

Then Green T went missing.

Archie returned to look for him. Twice. Searched the vampire manor, the surrounding territory, the tavern. Asked questions. Followed leads that went nowhere. Green T had vanished somewhere in the chaos of the anchor event and the dimensional instability that followed.

Archie spent time — SIGNIFICANT time, approximately three additional weeks — in the Shadowfell looking for Green T. He returned to the vampire manor and found the occupants had changed: the manor was immaculate now, restored, different. He could not get back inside. The situation had evolved without him.

He lived in the forest.

For a month.

Alone.

In the Shadowfell.

Waluigi has written about Archie's psychological resilience elsewhere. This is the event that proves it most clearly. Not the dinner, not the fireball, not the weeks of cover identity. A month of solitary existence in a dimension designed to extinguish hope, maintaining operational intent — finding Green T, getting home — without support, without allies, without fire for most of it.

Eventually the manor 'flashed.' The walls crumbled. Archie found himself back in the mirror room of the ruined material-plane Raventree Manor.

The Shadowfell had finally decided to spit him out.

summary: Archie Miser woke up on a marble floor in a world drained of all color—the Shadowfell, where entropy eats magic like dry soil eats water. His fire was GONE. Snap after snap produced nothing but cold grey smoke. Bowser called him 'candle-man,' which Waluigi finds hilarious but would never say to Archie's face. A pale-skinned, red-eyed butler toad led them to a dining hall of gothic opulence where Orangus Cornelius—a vampire toad with sharp fangs and a goblet of thick red liquid—waited at the head of an ebony table. Raw dripping meat was served. Bowser ate his in one bite. Green T had been placed at the CHILDREN'S TABLE wearing a BIB. And then Cornelius made the mistake of threatening Bowser's shell, Green T revealed a hidden flintlock pistol, and the dinner became a warzone that ended with Bowser wrestling a giant bat in the courtyard and a purple crystal shattering inside a hollow statue. The most significant dinner party Waluigi has ever heard about, and Waluigi was NOT THERE. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is reconstructing this event from testimony provided by Archie, Green T, and Bowser at various points after the fact. Their accounts are remarkably consistent, which either means it happened exactly as described or all three agreed on a story beforehand. Waluigi suspects the former—the details are too absurd to be coordinated fiction.

## The Cold Awakening — Day 21, Approximately 02:00


Archie Miser woke up on a marble floor that should have been wood. Everything around him was grey—black, white, shades of grey, no color anywhere. The Shadowfell had claimed him during the Planar Fracture, and it had taken his most important possession: his fire.

Archie tried to snap a flame into existence. Nothing. Snap again. A tiny spark appeared and instantly died—consumed by the Shadowfell's entropy. He tried a fireball. Nothing. Just a puff of cold grey smoke.

Waluigi has documented Archie's relationship with fire extensively. Fire is not merely Archie's weapon—it is his IDENTITY. The pyromaniac without pyromancy is like Waluigi without tennis. Technically functional. Spiritually devastated.

Bowser, who had been cast into the Shadowfell alongside Archie, reacted to the dimensional displacement with characteristic pragmatism. He stood up, looked around, punched a wall (which cracked without sound—even acoustics behaved wrong here), and asked 'Where are we?'

Bowser then laughed at Archie's magical impotence. 'Looks like you're out of fuel, candle-man.' Waluigi WISHES he could have witnessed this.

## The Butler and the


Invitation

A toad in a tuxedo appeared from the shadows. Pale grey skin. Red eyes. The demeanor of someone who has served drinks to the undead for so long that nothing surprises him anymore.

'Master Cornelius is expecting you.'

Bowser roared that he was KING BOWSER and demanded to know who Cornelius was. The butler did not flinch. 'The master does not like loud noises. Please follow me for the main course.'

Archie whispered to Bowser: 'Play along. I have no magic.' Bowser grumbled his agreement but promised that if the food was bad, he would burn the place down. Archie pointed out that Bowser couldn't burn anything either. Bowser reminded everyone that he had FISTS.

## The Dining Hall — Gothic Excess


The dining hall was a mirror of Raventree Manor's equivalent, twisted into something from a nightmare penned by an aristocrat. An ebony table polished to glass. High-backed chairs like thrones. Chandeliers dripping wax that looked suspiciously like coagulated blood.

Seated around the table: vampires, shades, pale nobles of the Onyx Hand. Figures of elegance and dread. The kind of dinner guests who consider 'still breathing' a fashion faux pas.

At the head of the table sat Orangus Cornelius. A Toad—but tall, which is unusual for Toads and deeply unnerving in context. Orange skin that would have been orange if color existed in this dimension. Sharp fangs. A goblet of thick red liquid that he held with the casual authority of someone who has been drinking blood for centuries.

'Welcome, guests. You are late.'

Bowser sat at the other end of the table. 'Nice place. A bit gloomy.'

Cornelius smiled. 'We prefer the term atmospheric.'

And then Archie noticed the CHILDREN'S TABLE.

## Green T at the Children's Table —


The Setup

Green T was seated at a small side table. Wearing a BIB. This was intended as a calculated insult—a dismissal of someone the vampires considered beneath the dignity of adult conversation.

Waluigi has written extensively about Green T in his dedicated entry, but the children's table detail adds a layer of humiliation that makes what happened next even MORE satisfying.

Green T looked terrified. He made eye contact with Archie. He tapped his spoon against the table—nervous energy, not morse code. Then he moved his hand under the table.

He flashed a gun. A flintlock. Where did he get a firearm? How did he smuggle it into a vampire dinner party? These questions have NEVER been satisfactorily answered, and Waluigi NEEDS to know.

## The Dinner Conversation — Debts and Threats


Servants brought out plates. Raw meat. Dripping.

Bowser ate his in one bite. 'Good steak. A bit rare.'

Archie stared at his plate. Cornelius insisted he eat—rudeness to a host was not tolerated. Archie claimed he wasn't hungry.

Cornelius escalated. He stood. He walked closer. He accused Archie of burning his greenhouse in the Material Plane. He spoke of a debt owed—glass designed to hold sunlight in a dimension that never sees sun.

Bowser stood up in Archie's defense. 'He owes you nothing, frog-face.'

Cornelius's response was the mistake that ended the dinner: 'Sit down, turtle. Or I will turn your shell into a soup bowl.'

YOU DO NOT THREATEN BOWSER'S SHELL.

The vampires hissed. Weapons were drawn. The diplomatic situation was collapsing. Archie tried to negotiate—'We can make a deal.'

Cornelius asked what Archie could possibly offer. Magic gone. Friends scattered. Nothing of value.

Green T stood up from the children's table.

'He has me.'

Cornelius looked at the small Toad with the bib. 'Sit down, pet.'

Green T pointed the gun.

'I said—he has me. And I have the key.'

'What key?'

'The key to the anchor.'

Cornelius's face dropped. Whatever the anchor was, whatever the key meant, it was significant enough to terrify a centuries-old vampire lord.

'Seize him.'

## The Standoff — Day 23

Green T kicked the children's table over. 'RUN, ARCHIE!'

Bowser flipped the MAIN table. Plates flew. Vampires screamed. The dinner party became a battlefield.

Archie grabbed a silver candlestick—silver burns vampires, basic monster-hunting knowledge—and swung it. It connected. The vampire hissed and burned.

Bowser tackled Cornelius. They crashed through a window into the courtyard. Green T fired—the shot brought down a chandelier. Archie screamed for the exit. Green T screamed that they had to break the mirror in the attic.

But Bowser was outside. Wrestling what had become a GIANT BAT—Cornelius's true form, apparently, because vampires are not content with merely being terrifying in humanoid shape.

Archie jumped out the window after Bowser. Gravity was lower in the Shadowfell—he floated down and landed on Bowser's shell.

Bowser BIT the bat's wing. Waluigi needs this repeated: BOWSER BIT A GIANT UNDEAD BAT. The immune system confidence required for this act is beyond mortal comprehension.

Cornelius screeched. Archie tried desperately to spark a spell—any spell. Not fire. Just light. Just a spark.

Fizzle. Nothing. Useless.

Bowser threw Cornelius into a statue. The statue broke. It was hollow. Inside: a crystal. Purple. Glowing.

Archie realized what it was. 'That's the anchor! SMASH IT, BOWSER!'

Bowser wound up a punch. Cornelius recovered—lunged—screamed 'NOOO!'

Time slowed. Green T appeared at the window above. He aimed the flintlock. He fired.

The bullet hit the crystal.

SHATTER.

The world cracked. Color bled in. Red. Orange. FIRE returned.

Archie felt heat in his hands for the first time since waking in the Shadowfell.

He smiled.

**Ignite.**

WAH.

summary: The Shadow Anchor was a purple crystal hidden inside a hollow statue in the Shadow Estate courtyard—a planar anchor that sustained the Shadowfell fragment's suppressive properties, draining color and dampening magic. When Bowser threw the vampire lord Orangus Cornelius into the statue and it shattered, the crystal was exposed. Green T, firing from a window above, put a silver bullet through it. The crystal shattered. Color bled back into the world. Fire returned to Archie's hands. The Shadowfell's grip on the fragment loosened. In one shot, Green T changed the conditions of the entire dimensional conflict. Waluigi maintains that this single moment—the children's table nobody shooting the crystal that held a dimension in darkness—is the most cinematically perfect event of the entire campaign. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is documenting the Shattering as a separate event from the dinner because its consequences extend far beyond one dinner party. The Shadow Anchor's destruction changed the fundamental conditions of the Shadowfell fragment.

## What the Shadow Anchor Was


The Shadow Anchor was a planar anchor—a crystal that stabilized the Shadowfell fragment's connection to Raventree Manor's dimensional structure. It also sustained the suppressive properties that made the Shadowfell so hostile to the living: the entropy that consumed magic, the color drain, the dampened sound.

The crystal was hidden inside a hollow statue in the courtyard—concealed within the estate's architecture where casual visitors would never find it. Waluigi suspects the Corvinarus family placed it there deliberately. The suppressive environment served their interests—vampires who don't need fire magic benefit enormously from a dimension where fire magic doesn't work.

## The Sequence of Destruction


The Anchor's destruction was not planned. It was the result of cascading chaos:

1. **Bowser tackled Cornelius through the dining hall window** because Cornelius threatened his shell.
2. **Bowser threw Cornelius into the courtyard statue** during their fight.
3. **The statue broke** because it was hollow—it had been constructed around the Anchor crystal.
4. **Archie recognized the crystal** as a planar anchor and screamed for Bowser to smash it.
5. **Cornelius lunged to prevent destruction** — the crystal was essential to his domain's power.
6. **Green T appeared at a window above** and fired his flintlock.
7. **The bullet hit the crystal.** It shattered.

Seven steps of unplanned escalation leading to a decisive moment. Nobody planned this sequence. It happened because Bowser is strong, statues are breakable, Archie recognizes magical artifacts, and Green T had a gun nobody knew about.

## The Immediate Effects


When the Anchor shattered:

**Color returned.** The grey, monochrome world of the Shadowfell fragment suddenly BLED with color. Red. Orange. Purple. The visual shock was reportedly disorienting for everyone present—Archie described it as 'like someone turned the world back on.'

**Magic resumed.** The entropy that had been consuming magical energy dissipated. Archie's fire returned. He felt heat in his hands for the first time since arriving in the Shadowfell. His smile when fire sparked from his fingers was reportedly the happiest anyone had ever seen him.

**The suppressive field collapsed.** Sound returned to normal volume. Gravity normalized. The Shadowfell's oppressive weight lifted—not entirely, but enough to make the fragment survivable rather than slowly lethal.

**Cornelius was weakened.** The vampire lord had been drawing power from the Anchor. Its destruction diminished him. He survived, but was severely injured between the bullet's effects and Bowser's physical assault.

## Cascading Consequences


The Anchor's destruction had effects beyond the immediate courtyard:

**The Shadow Estate destabilized.** Without the Anchor maintaining the fragment's properties, the estate began experiencing fluctuations. Rooms shifted. Passages that had been stable became unreliable. The vampires' carefully maintained environment was disrupted.

**Archie's magic became volatile.** When fire returned to Archie, it returned AGGRESSIVELY. His magical signature—already unstable before the Planar Fracture—became even more chaotic. The Mages' Guild later described him as 'bleeding entropy,' suggesting the Anchor's destruction and Archie's magic interacted in ways that amplified his instability.

**The Onyx Hand's position weakened.** Without the suppressive field, the Shadow Estate became accessible to threats that the environment had previously neutralized. The vampires could no longer rely on entropy to protect them from magical opposition.

**The fragment's connection to other planes shifted.** Archie's later encounters with Mages' Guild operatives revealed that the Anchor's destruction contributed to further planar instability. The bridge between the Shadowfell fragment and the material plane became more permeable.

## Green T's Shot —


The Moment That Mattered

Waluigi has written extensively about Green T elsewhere. But this moment deserves specific attention.

Green T was put at the children's table. He was given a bib. He was dismissed as irrelevant by centuries-old vampires who considered themselves masters of their domain.

And from that position of absolute dismissal, he produced a weapon nobody knew he had, aimed at a target nobody else could have reached, and fired the shot that changed everything.

The children's table shot the host's power source.

Waluigi WISHES he could have seen Cornelius's face. The fraction of a second between 'the crystal is exposed' and 'the crystal is destroyed.' The comprehension that the most dangerous person in the room was the small Toad with the bib.

How did Green T smuggle a flintlock into a vampire dinner party? Waluigi has asked. Green T has not answered. The mystery persists. Waluigi considers it one of the great unanswered questions of the campaign.

WAH.

Markop had been knocked unconscious previously and was being dragged by Bowser when Vivian attacked. Bowser held a door shut against axe blows. Markop regained consciousness just in time to fight. Then Vivian revealed why the Shadowfell's magic suppression didn't apply to them: 'The Shadowfell suppresses magic, but not THIS magic.' A crimson beam of disintegration hit Markop with enough force to destroy him. He survived because he whispered a prayer and his god answered with a divine shield. His armor barely held. Vivian's spell components were scattered and burned. Bowser found a necromancer's wand on the floor and asked 'Is this a magic wand?' with the innocent curiosity of a child finding a toy. The most Bowser moment of the entire campaign. WAH.
description:
Waluigi is documenting this fight because it represents two things simultaneously: the closest Markop has come to dying during the entire crisis, and the most perfectly characteristic Bowser moment Waluigi has ever heard described.

## The Setup — Dragged to Safety


Markop was unconscious. The details of how he was knocked out are unclear from Waluigi's sources, but the result was Bowser dragging him through stone corridors by the tail while Vivian Corvinarus pursued them.

Dragging an unconscious lizardfolk through stone corridors is not gentle. It is not dignified. But it is EFFECTIVE, and Bowser prioritized getting Markop out over performing rescue elegantly.

Markop woke up being dragged. 'What happened? I was with Remi and you came in—'

Bowser, still dragging: 'Running away from that guy.'

Banging on the door behind them.

Markop surveyed the room—a maintenance space packed with gardening tools and produce. Bowser was holding the door. An axe was thrown through it.

'It's not going to hold forever,' Bowser noted with characteristic understatement.

## The Breach


Vivian entered. Blinding smoke preceded them. Markop deflected it and moved outside—taking the fight to the corridor rather than remaining trapped.

Bowser knocked Vivian in the head as they entered. A solid hit that staggered the attacker.

Markop slashed with his battle axe. Vivian bled—red, through robes—but LAUGHED.

They fell to their knees. Not in defeat. In preparation.

## The Death Beam


Vivian's declaration was chilling in its casual revelation: 'Did you know the Shadowfell suppresses magic? But not THIS magic.'

A crimson beam of disintegration erupted. Not fire. Not lightning. Pure destructive energy that the Shadowfell's entropy could not dampen because it operated on different principles.

The beam hit Markop.

Markop has survived giant spiders. He has grown to titan size and wrestled building-scale arachnids. He has navigated the Deep Mirror—a dying dimension of decaying time. He has fought consistently, effectively, and with tactical brilliance throughout the crisis.

The death beam nearly ended all of it.

Markop felt himself at death's door. His armor—already stressed from previous engagements—buckled under the assault. The energy was consuming him.

And then Markop prayed.

Not a rehearsed invocation. Not a prepared spell. A WHISPERED prayer—the kind of prayer that happens in the fraction of a second between impact and annihilation, when the conscious mind has already accepted death and something deeper reaches out.

His god answered.

A divine shield formed. Golden light against crimson destruction. The beam's energy was absorbed—not entirely, not easily, but ENOUGH. Markop survived when survival should have been impossible.

## The Aftermath — Tactical Even at Death's Door


Markop's first action after surviving divine intervention was TACTICAL. He scattered and burned Vivian's spell components—the materials needed to cast the death beam again. Not revenge. Not panic. COUNTERPLAY. Even at the edge of death, Markop's combat instincts prioritized removing the enemy's capabilities.

Vivian was staggered by the component loss. The death beam was their trump card, and it had been neutralized.

## Bowser's Wand Discovery


During the chaos, something fell from Vivian. A wand. Dark. Cold to the touch.

Bowser picked it up. Turned it over curiously.

'Ooooh. Is this a magic wand?'

The party had nearly died. Markop's armor was failing. Divine intervention had been required. And Bowser found a necromantic artifact and examined it like a toddler discovering something interesting on the ground.

Markop—still recovering—managed: 'I'm not sure.'

Remi later confirmed it was indeed a necromancer's wand—death-aspected, cold to the touch. Bowser's casual handling of it may have been the safest possible outcome. Can you corrupt someone who doesn't understand they're supposed to be corrupted?

## The

Interrogation — What Vivian Revealed

Vivian was subsequently captured and interrogated by Markop and Bowser. The interrogation revealed:

**Vivian was not a Corvinarus by blood.** They had arrived at the manor disguised as 'Vivinessa'—a thrall—and worked their way close to the heir through deception. The wig was fake. The identity was constructed.

**Vivian's goal was sole inheritance.** They intended to kill both Orangus Cornelius and Kyrn Corvinarus, becoming the sole heir to the Shadow Estate.

**The blight plan.** Vivian had been 'blighting' manor residents—a form of corruption that would eventually give them control over the entire population. The Mazebounds in the grove were victims of this blight.

**Vivian wanted to close the planar fractures.** Not to restore normality, but to ISOLATE the Shadow Estate from outside influence, making themselves the sole controller of an enclosed dimensional pocket.

Three things had changed since the dinner that prompted Vivian's attack. They declined to specify what those three things were, leaving that mystery for the party to solve.

WAH.

description:
Waluigi is documenting the Mazebound Skirmish because it involved multiple party members, revealed important intelligence about Archie's movements, and demonstrated that the Shadow Estate's dangers extended well beyond the vampires inside the manor.

## The Mazebounds — What


They Were

Mazebounds were hunched, grey-skinned humanoids that lurked in the Shadow Estate's hedge maze and surrounding grove. Snub-nosed. Glowing white eyes. Long sharp nails that clicked and scraped with every movement. They moved through the hedges like they were PART of them—appearing and disappearing without warning.

The singing was the disturbing part. Mazebounds didn't simply attack—they PERFORMED. Choreographed entrances. Jazz hands. Musical numbers with lyrics about their territory, their victims, and their intentions. As if someone had combined undead predators with dinner theatre.

Waluigi has encountered many threats during this crisis. Vampires are terrifying but dignified. Dragons are apocalyptic but comprehensible. Singing hedge monsters who do jazz hands while trying to eat you are in a category of horror that Waluigi did not know existed.

## The


Initial Encounter — Musical Ambush

The party—Markop, Remi, Dan, Bowser, Salam, Eager—entered the maze searching for the greenhouse and following leads about Archie's whereabouts.

The Mazebounds burst from the bushes mid-song:

*'Welcome to the grove! Welcome to the gray! You'll never find the fountain, so you might as well stay!'*

Jazz hands. Actual jazz hands.

Remi's response was to follow Salam as he grabbed her and ran into the bushes. Markop was seized and dragged. The party was separated—exactly as the Mazebounds intended.

The Mazebounds performed a rapid patter song about their tactical approach:

*'Check the Turtle! Big and loud! Crack the shell to please the crowd! Check the Archer! Check the Whip! Watch them stumble, watch them slip!'*

Waluigi finds it deeply disturbing that monsters have developed tactical musical numbers. This is not how combat is supposed to work.

## Archie's Artifacts — Evidence of Prior Passage


During the maze exploration, the party discovered several items belonging to Archie Miser:

**The Third Eye Circlet** — A brass circlet inscribed with 'The eye sees across—the band keeps me from falling in.' It vibrated near mirrors and planar boundaries.

**The Component Pouch** — Archie's emergency spell components, labeled 'For When Everything Goes to Hell (again)' in his bitterly self-aware handwriting.

**A Wahwire Tablet** — Cracked, smudged, displaying fragments of text when touched. It greeted the finder as 'Welcome Archie Miser to Wahwire.'

These artifacts confirmed that Archie had passed through the maze—and had lost or abandoned his equipment along the way. Whether he dropped them while fleeing Mazebounds or left them deliberately as breadcrumbs remains unclear.

## Dan's Capture and Rescue


Dan was seized by Mazebounds and dragged into the deeper grove. The creatures constricted him, singing as they pulled:

*'But the dance has just begun! And you're the guest of honor, son!'*

Two crossbow bolts—fired from an unknown position—struck the Mazebounds holding Dan. They retreated. Dan was freed.

The unknown benefactor later revealed themselves briefly, describing their assistance as 'enlightened pragmatism' and 'tactical investment.' Their identity and affiliation remain unclear. They fired bolts that saved party members but offered no further assistance.

## The Grove — What


They Found

Deeper in the maze, the party discovered the central grove:

A towering dead tree with vast branches forming a massive canopy. Dozens of corpses hung from those branches by their necks. Hundreds of shadow crows with crimson eyes sat in the boughs, offering 'waves of grating mockery.' The trunk was twisted to create a skull-like visage with glowing eyes that tracked movement.

Ragged stone obelisks jutted from the earth around the tree, marked with glowing sigils that caused stomach-churning nausea when viewed.

Waluigi would like it on record that he is GRATEFUL he was in the Feywild dealing with fairy politics instead of encountering a corpse tree guarded by singing hedge monsters.

## The Escape


The party escaped the maze through a combination of Bowser's fire breath (clearing hedges), Remi cutting directly through walls with her dagger, and sheer determination. The Mazebounds eventually ceased pursuit when the party left the grove's boundaries.

The maze revealed that the Shadow Estate's grounds were as dangerous as the manor itself—possibly MORE dangerous, since the vampires at least maintained social protocols. The Mazebounds maintained nothing except musical numbers and territorial violence.

WAH.
